name: Hukaung Valley Tiger Reserve
blurb: Myanmar's largest reserve: tigers, deer, elephants and fig forest.

tip.title: Thin out the sambar
tip.text: Sambar are a favourite prey of tigers. Set Sambar to -80% and watch the tiger, dhole and leopard, then the crows that scavenge their kills.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Rattan palms
nodes.desc: Climbing, spiny palms of the forest understorey. Many Calamus species are recorded in the Hukaung area, including one named for it.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit through much of the year in tropical forests, so they feed hornbills, monkeys, deer and many other animals.

nodes.name: Forest grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and reeds of clearings and river flats give grazers a main food in the valley bottom.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: A huge browser and grazer that eats grasses, palms and bark and opens paths through dense forest. Calves can fall to tigers.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A large deer that eats grasses, leaves and fruit and stays near water. It is a favourite prey of tigers.

nodes.name: Indian muntjac
nodes.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and picks up fallen fruit. Tigers and leopards take it.

nodes.name: Shortridge's langur
nodes.desc: An endangered leaf-eating monkey of northern Myanmar forests that lives in the canopy and feeds on leaves and fruit.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for fruit, tubers and invertebrates, and is hunted by tigers and dholes.

nodes.name: Oriental pied hornbill
nodes.desc: A large forest bird that eats figs and other fruit as well as lizards and insects, and so spreads fig seeds.

nodes.name: Crow butterflies
nodes.desc: Forest butterflies whose caterpillars feed on plants such as figs. Adults and young are food for lizards.

nodes.name: Dhole
nodes.desc: A pack-hunting wild dog that takes deer and boar. Tigers can steal its kills and push packs away.

nodes.name: Clouded leopard
nodes.desc: A tree-climbing cat recorded in camera-trap surveys of Hukaung, thought to take deer and monkeys.

nodes.name: Crested serpent eagle
nodes.desc: A forest raptor that hunts snakes and lizards from perches under the canopy and is one of the best-recorded birds nearby.

nodes.name: Variable agama
nodes.desc: An insect-eating lizard of forest edges and gardens. Birds and snakes prey on it.

nodes.name: White-lipped pit viper
nodes.desc: A tree-dwelling venomous snake that ambushes lizards and other small animals.

nodes.name: Large-billed crow
nodes.desc: A bold omnivore that scavenges carcasses, including the leftovers of big-cat kills, and also takes small animals.

nodes.name: Tiger
nodes.desc: The reserve was set up to protect tigers. They hunt large deer and wild pigs and need big, connected forest.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Camera traps show leopards here. They hunt medium prey such as muntjac and langurs, and live alongside tigers.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Tropical sun powers year-round growth in the evergreen forest.

nodes.name: Monsoon rains
nodes.desc: Heavy monsoon rain feeds the rivers and keeps the forest evergreen.

nodes.name: Chindwin headwaters
nodes.desc: The Tanai and other streams drain the valley and form the head of the Chindwin River, watering the lowlands.

nodes.name: Valley soils
nodes.desc: Alluvial valley soils and forest litter supply nutrients to the plants.

nodes.name: Fungi & termites
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
